comparator.name: Bachelor Applied Mathematics
comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 current programme and course records; official 180-EC structure checked 2026-10-06
comparator.sourceNotes: The current TU/e programme and degree-structure material identifies a three-year, 180-EC Applied Mathematics bachelor. The governing Bachelor College directive accounts for the complete degree as a 125-EC core, including a 10-, 15- or 20-EC Bachelor Final Project, 45 EC of elective space and 10 EC of Impact of Technology. Current 2026-2027 course records substantiate the programme's cumulative proof-based and applied formation in calculus and analysis, linear algebra and algebraic structures, discrete mathematics and graph theory, ordinary differential equations and numerical analysis, probability, statistics and measure theory, optimisation, modelling and programming, professional skills and a mathematics-specific Bachelor Final Project. No named route or specialisation is required for the normalized target, and genuine elective space is preserved rather than populated with invented choices.
components: Applied Mathematics core programme, including Bachelor Final Project

Compulsory formation in mathematical language and proof, calculus and analysis, linear algebra and algebraic structures, graph theory and discrete mathematics, ordinary differential equations, numerical analysis and scientific computing, probability, statistics and measure theory, stochastic modelling, optimisation, programming and modelling projects, professional skills, and the Bachelor Final Project.
Genuine elective space preserved from the official Bachelor College structure.
Required Engineering Ethics and Engineering for Society formation.

exception.reason: Applied Mathematics at TU/e is a cumulative proof-based mathematics degree. Its core develops mathematical language and proof alongside calculus and analysis, linear algebra and algebraic structures, discrete mathematics and graph theory, ordinary differential equations and numerical methods, probability, statistics and measure theory, stochastic modelling, optimisation, programming and repeated mathematical modelling before a discipline-specific Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers a useful applied mathematics, statistics, programming and data-science sequence, but it does not provide the sustained proof-intensive analysis, measure theory, abstract algebra, discrete-mathematics breadth and mathematics-specific research environment required to preserve this degree's academic identity. A 24-course UCR response would become an interdisciplinary quantitative and data-science pathway rather than Applied Mathematics.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official structure accounts for the full 180 EC as a 125-EC Applied Mathematics core including the Bachelor Final Project, 45 EC of genuine elective space and 10 EC of Impact of Technology. Current 2026-2027 course records substantiate calculus specifically for Applied Mathematics, probability and modelling, Lebesgue integration and measure-theoretic probability, stochastic and industrial modelling, professional formation and a mathematics-specific final project. The current catalogue also records the 2026-2027 replacement of the generic Calculus Variant 3 with Calculus for Applied Mathematics, confirming that the curriculum evidence applies to the present academic year. These elements form a connected proof, modelling and application progression rather than a set of optional quantitative courses.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide meaningful applied quantitative foundations. DISARIN212 Logic & Discrete Mathematics adds formal logic and discrete structures, while DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming and DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science, DISDATA211 Machine Learning and DISDATA311 Advanced Data Analysis add programming, data science and statistical computation. The workbook nevertheless has no sustained proof-based sequence in real and complex analysis, measure theory, abstract algebra or topology; no dedicated graph-theory, stochastic-process, mathematical-optimisation or partial-differential-equations sequence; and no mathematics-specific independent research project comparable to the Bachelor Final Project. The available courses support a coherent interdisciplinary applied-mathematics and data-science pathway, but cannot supply the target's dense compulsory pure-and-applied mathematics progression without replacing its defining upper mathematics with adjacent computing and data-science study.
